html:
The Treaty of Verdun, agreed in August 843, split the Carolingian Empire of Charlemagne among his three surviving grandsons. It is often taken as the starting point of France and Germany.

After their father Louis the Pious died in 840, the brothers fought a civil war. At Verdun they agreed:

  • Charles the Bald took West Francia, which grew into France.
  • Louis the German took East Francia, the core of later Germany.
  • Lothair kept the title of emperor and a long middle kingdom from the Low Countries to Italy, holding both Aachen and Rome.

The middle kingdom soon broke up. Its northern part, Lotharingia, gave its name to Lorraine, and the lands between France and Germany stayed a fought-over borderland into the 20th century. The treaty ended the single realm of the Franks.
